title: Calculate and interpret a p-value
show: normal curve centred on 500 with the sample mean marked and the tail area shaded

example.question: A machine is set to fill bags with a mean mass of $500$ g and a standard deviation of $12$ g. A sample of $36$ bags has a mean mass of $504.6$ g. Test, at the $5\%$ level, whether the mean mass has changed. Use a $p$-value.
example.final: p = 0.0214 < 0.05 \text{, so the mean mass has changed}

steps.say: Standardise the sample mean to find $\hl{1}{z}$. The spread of a sample mean is $\sigma/\sqrt{n}$, not $\sigma$.
Look up $P(z < 2.3)$ in the normal tables.
The test is two-tailed, so $\hl{2}{p}$ counts both tails. Take the tail above $2.3$ and double it.
Compare $\hl{2}{p}$ with $0.05$. Then say what it means for the claim, in the words of the question.

rows.aside: $p$ is less than $0.05$, so reject the claim. There is evidence that the mean mass of the bags has changed.

title: Standardise a value
show: normal curve mean 58 sd 12 with the shaded area for the asked mark

example.question: The marks in an exam are normally distributed with mean $58$ and standard deviation $12$. Find the percentage of students who scored more than $73$.

steps.say: Standardise: take away the mean, then divide by the standard deviation. This gives $\hl{1}{z}$.
The tables give the area to the **left** of $z$. Look up $P(z < 1.25)$.
We want the students above $73$, so take the left area from $1$.

rows.aside: About $10.6\%$ of the students scored more than $73$.

title: Make decisions with the empirical rule
show: normal curve mean 60 sd 5 with 1, 2 and 3 sd bands marked 68%, 95%, 99.7%

example.question: The lifetime of a battery is normally distributed with mean $60$ hours and standard deviation $5$ hours. Use the empirical rule to find the percentage of batteries that last more than $70$ hours.

steps.say: Find how far $70$ is above the mean, then divide by $\sigma$. This is how many $\hl{1}{\sigma}$ away it is.

rows.aside: So $70$ is $2$ standard deviations above the mean.

steps.say: The empirical rule says $95\%$ of values lie within $2$ standard deviations of the mean. That is between $50$ and $70$ hours.
The rest lies outside, in the two tails. We want only the **upper** tail, so split it in half.

title: Read probabilities from normal tables
show: normal curve mean 500 sd 8 with the required area shaded

example.question: The mass of a bag of sugar is normally distributed with mean $500$ g and standard deviation $8$ g. Find the probability that a bag has mass greater than $512$ g.

steps.say: Standardise $512$. Subtract the mean, then divide by the standard deviation. This gives $\hl{1}{z}$.
The tables give $P(z < \hl{1}{1.5})$, the area to the **left**. Find $1.5$ down the side and read across.
We want the area to the **right** of $\hl{1}{1.5}$. The whole area is $1$, so take away $\hl{2}{0.9332}$.

title: Work backwards from a normal probability
show: normal curve mean 58 sd 9 with the top 20% tail shaded and the cut-off marked

example.question: The marks in an exam are normally distributed with mean $58$ and standard deviation $9$. The top $20\%$ of students get a distinction. Find the lowest mark that gets a distinction, to the nearest whole number.

steps.say: Top $20\%$ means $80\%$ of students are below the cut-off. So the left area is $0.8$.
Look **inside** the table for the area closest to $0.8$. Read $\hl{1}{z}$ from the edge.
Put $\hl{1}{0.84}$, the mean and the standard deviation into $z = \frac{x - \mu}{\sigma}$. Then solve for $\hl{2}{x}$.
The question wants a whole mark. $65$ would be just short, so round up to $66$.

title: Use radian measure
show: sector radius 6 cm angle 150°=5π/6 with the arc marked

example.question: A sector of a circle has radius $6$ cm and angle $150^\circ$. (i) Write $150^\circ$ in radians. (ii) Find the area of the sector, in terms of $\pi$.

steps.say: Multiply the angle in degrees by $\frac{\pi}{180}$. Cancel the fraction.
The sector area formula $\frac{1}{2}r^2\theta$ needs $\theta$ in **radians**. Use $\hl{1}{\frac{5\pi}{6}}$, not $150$.
Put in $r = 6$ and $\theta = \hl{1}{\frac{5\pi}{6}}$.
